podcast.body: A single from the 1993 album *Zooropa*, "Numb" is notable for featuring The Edge on lead vocals, employing a deadpan rap style, rather than Bono. Bono provided falsetto background vocals. Drummer Larry Mullen Jr. contributed a melodic hook to the track and can also be heard vocally, possibly for the only time in a U2 song. The song's origins trace back to "Down All The Days," a rejected track from the *Achtung Baby* sessions. The Edge, who was going through a divorce at the time, developed the song's industrial feel, incorporating various sound effects including a video arcade, a rewinding Walkman, and a Hitler Youth kid playing a bass drum from the 1935 Nazi propaganda film *Triumph of the Will*. "Numb a single from you to his 1993 album Zuropa with the edge on vocals Bono does back up and so does Larry Moan"
